seo.title: LGW Airport Guide: London Gatwick Terminals & Transport | Tripways
seo.subheadline: London's second-busiest airport: terminals, Gatwick Express, and passenger tips
seo.meta_description: Complete passenger guide for London Gatwick Airport (LGW). Covers Gatwick Express, Thameslink, inter-terminal monorail, and flight advice.

faqs.answer: A free automated elevated shuttle runs 24 hours a day between North and South Terminals. The trip takes roughly 2 minutes with departures every few minutes.
faqs.question: How do I get between North Terminal and South Terminal at Gatwick?

steps.body: Both North and South Terminals have dedicated immigration halls with e-Passport gates and baggage reclaim carousels.
steps.title: 1. Passport Control & Baggage

steps.body: The railway station is integrated directly into South Terminal. Passengers landing at North Terminal take the 2-minute free monorail shuttle to South Terminal.
steps.title: 2. Gatwick Railway Station Access

arrival.summary: UK border inspection, baggage collection, and train station access at South Terminal.

lounges.name: No1 Lounge Gatwick
lounges.access_summary: Priority Pass, DragonPass, and walk-in pass
lounges.location_summary: Airside in North and South Terminals

notices.body: You can tap in and tap out with standard contactless payment cards or Oyster cards on all trains between Gatwick and Central London without buying paper tickets.
notices.title: Use Contactless for Train Tickets

steps.body: easyJet operates from both terminals. British Airways, Norse Atlantic, and Singapore Airlines operate from South Terminal. Emirates and Qatar Airways operate from North Terminal.
steps.title: 1. Terminal Confirmation

orientation.intro: London Gatwick Airport (LGW) is located 45 km south of Central London in West Sussex.
orientation.summary: Operating two terminals — North Terminal and South Terminal — connected by a free 24-hour automated monorail shuttle.
